posts.title: Reel: 30 new ads, Meta saw one (the first-frame test)
posts.hook: 30 new ads. Meta saw one.
posts.caption:
30 new ads. Meta saw one.

We looked at every new video ad the brands we work with launched from May to September 2026. New ads that looked like ads already running got 36% less first-month spend. A proven message in a new look got 47% more.

The test to run before your next launch: line up the first frame of every ad with the sound off. If you can't tell two apart, that is one ad. Launch one.

Read the full newsletter on our website, link in bio.

End card: read the full newsletter, link in bio.

posts.caption:
The sale is over. Before the ads get archived, write three lines.

1. The reason to buy your top-spending ads gave: discount, gift, deadline or bundle.
2. The first shot of each of those ads. Screenshot it.
3. The ads that got no spend, and what they had in common.

That is one page. It is also the brief for your next sale, and the Republic Day sales are closer than they look.

posts.title: Reel: the four-line creator brief
posts.hook: A creator brief that fits on one phone screen. Four lines.
posts.caption:
A creator brief that fits on one phone screen. Four lines.

1. Who it is for. One buyer, in plain words.
2. The one reason to buy.
3. The first shot: what viewers see first.
4. The one thing never to say or show.

Ten talking points can't fit in thirty seconds, so the creator ends up reading the brief aloud. Give them four lines and leave the rest to them. That is what you hired them for.

Save this for your next brief. Follow @galvor.ai.

posts.title: Reel: old competitor ad? Two checks before you copy it
posts.hook: That competitor ad has run for months. It still might not be working.
posts.caption:
That competitor ad has run for months. It still might not be working.

The ad library shows what is live. It does not show results, and an ad can stay on simply because nobody switched it off.

Two checks before you copy anything:
1. What do they keep remaking? New versions of one opening are a stronger hint than one old ad.
2. Does the same pattern show up across several brands in your category?

Then test it small, with your own reason to buy. Follow @galvor.ai.

posts.title: Reel: three rules our team works by
posts.hook: Three rules our team works by. All three are about ads.
posts.caption:
Three rules our team works by. All three are about ads.

1. A small sample is a signal. One good week earns a second test.
2. We price the attribute, not the ad. The hook, the cast and the pacing are each checked against cost per order.
3. Every ad should make the next one better. An ad that taught nothing cost more than its spend.

They are free to borrow for 2027. Follow @galvor.ai.

posts.title: Reel: three questions for any AI ad advice (meet Vira)
posts.hook: An AI tool says cut this ad. Ask it three questions first.
posts.caption:
An AI tool says cut this ad. Ask it three questions first.

1. What did you look at? Which ads, which dates?
2. What would you do: scale, cut or shift?
3. What result would prove you wrong?

If a tool can't answer, treat the advice as a guess.

Vira, Galvor's digital co-worker, shows its thinking with every call, so your team can check it before anyone acts. See Vira on galvor.ai, link in bio. Follow @galvor.ai.

posts.caption:
Three questions your ads dashboard can't answer.

1. What do our ten best ads have in common?
2. Which reason to buy have we stopped testing?

A dashboard is built for how much. A brief needs why, and what next.

Try answering these by hand for your last quarter. Or type them into Ask Galvor in plain words. Follow @galvor.ai.

posts.title: Reel: where a creator video loses its days
posts.hook: Where a creator video loses its days between brief and live.
posts.caption:
Where a creator video loses its days between brief and live.

The shoot gets blamed. Late feedback is the costlier part, because a rewrite is quick and a reshoot is slow.

Three checkpoints that move feedback to the front:
1. Approve the script on paper before any camera rolls.
2. Name one person who gives the feedback, in one round.
3. Judge the first cut against the brief, never against taste.

Feedback becomes a yes or a no, and the video goes live. Follow @galvor.ai.
